title: Microsoft Fabric Error-Rate Trend Anomaly
dataSources: Fabric capacity metrics (`fabric:capacity:metrics`) and admin API.
app: Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics app exports and the Fabric Admin API via HEC scripted inputs.
spl:
index=bi sourcetype=fabric:capacity:metrics
| bin _time span=1h
| stats count as events, sum(eval(status="Failure")) as errors by _time
| eval error_rate=round(100*errors/events,2)
| eventstats avg(error_rate) as avg_rate, stdev(error_rate) as sd_rate
| where error_rate>avg_rate+3*sd_rate
| sort - _time
description: Baselines the hourly error rate for Microsoft Fabric and flags hours where it spikes more than three standard deviations above normal, catching emerging instability before it becomes an outage.
value: An error-rate spike is the earliest signal that Microsoft Fabric is degrading; statistical baselining suppresses routine noise and pages only on genuine anomalies.
implementation: Ingest Microsoft Fabric logs into index=bi; schedule every 15 minutes over a trailing window and alert on 3-sigma error-rate anomalies.
visualization: Timechart of Microsoft Fabric error rate with anomaly band.
grandmaExplanation: We learn what a normal amount of Microsoft Fabric errors looks like and warn you only when something is genuinely going wrong.
